name: Stuxnet
description: First known cyberweapon targeting industrial control systems. Sabotaged Iranian nuclear centrifuges via Siemens PLCs.
root_cause: Zero-day exploits + supply chain compromise
lessons: ICS/OT networks require air-gapping and strict supply chain controls.

name: WannaCry Ransomware
description: Global ransomware attack exploiting NSA's EternalBlue SMB exploit. Hit 150+ countries, crippled UK NHS.
root_cause: Unpatched systems (MS17-010), no network segmentation
lessons: Patch management and network segmentation are non-negotiable.

name: SolarWinds SUNBURST
description: Trojanized SolarWinds Orion update compromised 18,000 organizations including US Treasury, DHS, and Fortune 500 companies.
root_cause: Supply chain compromise, insufficient code signing verification
lessons: Software supply chain integrity verification is critical. Zero-trust architecture needed.

name: Log4Shell (Log4j)
description: Critical RCE in Apache Log4j (CVE-2021-44228). CVSS 10.0. Affected billions of devices. Exploited within hours of disclosure.
root_cause: Insecure JNDI lookup in ubiquitous logging library
lessons: Dependency management and SBOMs are essential. Patch velocity matters.

name: MOVEit Transfer Mass Exploitation
description: Cl0p exploited zero-day SQL injection in MOVEit Transfer (CVE-2023-34362). 2,700+ organizations breached.
root_cause: SQL injection vulnerability in file transfer software
lessons: Third-party file transfer tools are high-value targets. Input validation is critical.

name: Target Data Breach
description: Attackers gained access via compromised HVAC vendor credentials, stole 40M credit cards and 70M customer records.
root_cause: Third-party vendor access, flat network, no segmentation
lessons: Third-party access must be strictly controlled and segmented.

name: Equifax Data Breach
description: Unpatched Apache Struts vulnerability exposed PII of 147M Americans including SSNs, DOBs, and credit card numbers.
root_cause: Unpatched known vulnerability (2 months old), poor asset inventory
lessons: Patch management and asset inventory are foundational security controls.

name: NotPetya
description: Destructive wiper disguised as ransomware. Spread via MeDoc accounting software update. Most costly cyberattack in history.
root_cause: Supply chain compromise + unpatched SMB
lessons: Destructive malware can masquerade as ransomware. Backups must be offline.

name: Colonial Pipeline Ransomware
description: DarkSide ransomware shut down largest US fuel pipeline for 6 days. $4.4M ransom paid. Fuel shortages across US East Coast.
root_cause: Reused/leaked VPN password, no MFA
lessons: MFA on all remote access is mandatory. OT/IT network separation critical.

name: Yahoo Data Breach
description: All 3 billion Yahoo accounts compromised. Largest data breach in history. Disclosed 2 years after breach.
root_cause: Weak MD5 hashing, no breach detection, delayed disclosure
lessons: Strong password hashing (bcrypt/Argon2) and breach detection are essential.

name: Sony Pictures Hack
description: Destructive attack wiped Sony's network, leaked unreleased films, executive emails, and employee PII. Politically motivated.
root_cause: Spear phishing, insufficient endpoint protection
lessons: Insider threat programs and data classification are critical for media companies.

name: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160)
description: Critical OpenSSL vulnerability allowed reading server memory, exposing private keys and passwords. Affected ~17% of internet.
root_cause: Buffer over-read bug in OpenSSL TLS heartbeat extension
lessons: Open source security auditing and rapid patch deployment are critical.

name: Mirai Botnet DDoS
description: Mirai botnet of 600,000 IoT devices took down Dyn DNS, disrupting Twitter, Netflix, Reddit, and major internet services.
root_cause: Default credentials on IoT devices, no IoT security standards
lessons: IoT devices must have unique credentials and firmware update mechanisms.

name: Uber Data Breach
description: Teen hacker used MFA fatigue attack on contractor, then pivoted via Slack to access AWS, GCP, and internal systems.
root_cause: MFA fatigue, over-privileged contractor access, poor secrets management
lessons: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) and least-privilege access are essential.

name: LastPass Breach
description: Attacker compromised developer laptop, stole source code, then used it to breach cloud storage containing encrypted password vaults.
root_cause: Compromised developer endpoint, insufficient secrets separation
lessons: Developer workstations are high-value targets. Secrets must be isolated from source code.

name: Conficker Worm
description: Conficker infected 9-15 million Windows machines, creating one of the largest botnets ever. Exploited unpatched Windows RPC.
root_cause: Unpatched Windows systems, weak passwords
lessons: Automated patch management and network monitoring are essential.

name: RSA SecurID Breach
description: APT1 stole seed values for RSA SecurID tokens, compromising two-factor authentication for millions of users worldwide.
root_cause: Spear phishing, unpatched Flash, insufficient network segmentation
lessons: Authentication infrastructure is a high-value target requiring extra protection.

name: Kaseya VSA Ransomware
description: REvil exploited zero-day in Kaseya VSA to push ransomware to 1,500+ businesses via MSPs. $70M ransom demanded.
root_cause: Zero-day in widely-used MSP software, supply chain amplification
lessons: MSP software is a force multiplier for attackers. Vendor security assessments are critical.

name: Twitter Bitcoin Scam
description: 17-year-old social engineered Twitter employees to access admin tools, hijacking accounts of Obama, Biden, Musk, Gates for Bitcoin scam.
root_cause: Insider threat, excessive admin tool access, phone-based social engineering
lessons: Privileged access to admin tools must require multi-party authorization.

name: Microsoft Exchange ProxyLogon
description: Four zero-days in Microsoft Exchange Server exploited by HAFNIUM and 10+ other APT groups. 250,000+ servers compromised.
root_cause: Unpatched on-premise Exchange servers, delayed patching
lessons: On-premise email servers are high-value targets. Cloud migration reduces attack surface.

name: Marriott/Starwood Breach
description: 500M Starwood guest records stolen over 4 years. Breach began in 2014 before Marriott acquisition. Included passport numbers.
root_cause: Undetected persistence for 4 years, insufficient M&A security due diligence
lessons: M&A security due diligence must include threat hunting. Detection time matters.

name: SamSam Ransomware (Atlanta)
description: SamSam ransomware crippled City of Atlanta for weeks. $51K ransom demanded, $17M in recovery costs.
root_cause: Exposed RDP with weak credentials, no offline backups
lessons: RDP must never be exposed to internet. Offline backups are essential for government.

name: Lazarus Group Bangladesh Bank Heist
description: $81M stolen from Bangladesh Bank via fraudulent SWIFT messages. $951M attempted. Exploited weak SWIFT security controls.
root_cause: Weak SWIFT security controls, no anomaly detection on transactions
lessons: Financial transaction monitoring and SWIFT security controls are critical.

name: Okta Breach via Lapsus$
description: Lapsus$ compromised Okta via third-party support provider Sitel, gaining access to customer admin consoles.
root_cause: Third-party vendor security, excessive support access
lessons: Identity providers require the highest security standards for all vendors.

name: 3CX Supply Chain Attack
description: Lazarus Group compromised 3CX VoIP software via a prior supply chain attack on Trading Technologies. First known supply chain attack via supply chain.
root_cause: Cascading supply chain compromise, insufficient binary signing verification
lessons: Supply chain attacks can cascade. SBOM and reproducible builds are essential.

name: MGM Resorts Ransomware
description: 10-minute LinkedIn/vishing attack on IT helpdesk led to Okta compromise, then ransomware across MGM's casino operations.
root_cause: Helpdesk social engineering, insufficient identity verification
lessons: Helpdesk identity verification must be rigorous. Vishing is a critical attack vector.

name: Change Healthcare Ransomware
description: Largest healthcare data breach in US history. Disrupted prescription processing for weeks. $22M ransom paid.
root_cause: No MFA on Citrix remote access, single point of failure in healthcare infrastructure
lessons: Healthcare critical infrastructure requires MFA everywhere and resilient architecture.

name: XZ Utils Backdoor
vector: Social engineering of open source maintainer
description: 2-year social engineering campaign inserted backdoor into XZ Utils compression library, targeting SSH authentication in Linux distros.
root_cause: Open source maintainer burnout exploited, insufficient code review
lessons: Open source supply chain security requires funded maintainers and automated analysis.

name: Snowflake Customer Breaches
description: Attackers used credentials stolen by infostealer malware to access 165+ Snowflake customer accounts with no MFA enabled.
root_cause: No MFA enforcement on cloud data platform, infostealer malware on employee devices
lessons: Cloud platforms must enforce MFA. Infostealer malware is a primary credential theft vector.

name: PowerSchool Data Breach
description: Attackers used stolen credentials to access PowerSchool's student information system, exposing data of 62M+ students and teachers across thousands of school districts in the US and Canada.
root_cause: No MFA on maintenance portal, credentials stolen via infostealer malware
lessons: Education sector SIS platforms hold sensitive PII for millions of minors and require MFA and strict access controls.

name: Oracle Cloud Breach
vector: Unauthenticated RCE in Oracle Access Manager
description: Threat actor claimed to have breached Oracle Cloud's SSO infrastructure, exfiltrating 6M records including encrypted SSO passwords and LDAP data from 140,000+ tenants. Oracle initially denied the breach.
root_cause: Unpatched Oracle Access Manager vulnerability (CVE-2021-35587), delayed disclosure
lessons: Cloud providers must patch critical auth infrastructure immediately. Transparent breach disclosure is essential.

name: Marks & Spencer Ransomware
description: Scattered Spider used social engineering to compromise M&S IT systems, disrupting online orders, contactless payments, and Click & Collect for weeks. Customer data including contact details and order history exposed.
root_cause: Helpdesk social engineering, insufficient identity verification for privileged access
lessons: Retail critical systems require phishing-resistant MFA and rigorous helpdesk verification. Scattered Spider continues targeting large enterprises.

name: Co-op Cyberattack
description: Co-op confirmed a significant cyberattack affecting back-office and call centre systems, with DragonForce ransomware group claiming responsibility and threatening to leak member data.
root_cause: Social engineering attack on IT helpdesk, same TTPs as M&S attack
lessons: Wave of UK retail attacks shows sector-wide vulnerability to social engineering. Industry-wide helpdesk security standards needed.

name: Bybit Crypto Heist
description: Lazarus Group compromised the Safe{Wallet} multisig interface used by Bybit, injecting malicious JavaScript to redirect a $1.5B ETH transfer. Largest crypto theft in history.
root_cause: Supply chain compromise of third-party wallet UI, insufficient transaction verification
lessons: Crypto platforms must verify transaction destinations out-of-band. Third-party UI dependencies are critical attack surfaces.

name: Harrods Cyberattack
description: Harrods confirmed it was the third major UK retailer targeted in weeks, restricting internet access to sites as a precautionary measure after detecting intrusion attempts.
root_cause: Same Scattered Spider TTPs targeting UK retail sector
lessons: Coordinated sector-targeting by threat actors requires industry-wide threat intelligence sharing and coordinated defenses.

name: Aurora Operation (Google)
description: Sophisticated APT campaign targeting Google, Adobe, and 30+ companies. Aimed at source code and Gmail accounts of Chinese dissidents.
root_cause: IE zero-day, spear phishing, insufficient network monitoring
lessons: Nation-state APTs target intellectual property. Defense-in-depth is essential.
